large.event: at least one large fire (1,000 acres or more on CAL FIRE's fire perimeter maps) that started in the month and reached the hexagon or county
large.method: Logistic regression on features computed only from years up to the forecast origin: the unit x calendar-month large-fire rate (+-1 month window; for hexagons also a Gaussian average over 2 rings of neighbours), the unit's any-month rate, a recency-weighted rate (half-life 5 years), the state seasonal rate, the unit's harmonized FIRMS hotspot history, and whether the unit had a large fire in the last 3 or 4-10 years. Separate fits for one year ahead (2026) and two years ahead (2027), trained on forecast origins 2005 onward. Hexagons and counties are fitted separately.
large.is_forecast: A statistical outlook from fire history alone: no weather, fuel moisture or ignitions. It cannot know whether 2026 or 2027 will be a big fire year; its value is in ranking places and months. The backtest shows it barely beats the state's seasonal average on Brier score and ranks places far better than history alone.

backtest.design: Rolling origin. Each test year Y in 2018-2025 is forecast with data through Y-1 (horizon 1) or Y-2 (horizon 2), refitting the model each time on outcomes known by then. Baselines get the same data. 'history_alone': share of years 2001..origin with a large fire in that unit and calendar month. 'state_seasonal_average': the average over all units for that calendar month. Log loss clips every forecast to [floor, 1-floor] so history-alone zeros can be scored. top_N_pct: share of the test year's large-fire unit-months that fell in that year's N% highest forecasts. expected_vs_observed_by_year: [sum of forecasts, actual count].

past.pairs_layout: flat pairs: hexagon index (BURN_DATA.states.CA.hexes rows), month index i = (year-2001)*12 + (month-1)
past.county_rows_layout: flat rows of four: county index (data.js states.CA.counties), month index, large fires, acres in county

large.definition: A large fire is a CAL FIRE FRAP perimeter of at least 1,000 acres (GIS_ACRES, the mapped area, including any part outside California), years 2001-2025, dated by the month of ALARM_DATE, or of CONT_DATE when the alarm date is missing.
large.hex_rule: A hexagon is marked for a month when a large fire that started that month covers at least 1% of it (about 1.6 km2) or the hexagon holds that fire's largest share.
large.county_rule: A fire counts in a county when at least 1% of its mapped area is in that county, or the county holds its largest share. A fire crossing counties counts once in each, so county totals add up to more than the state total. acres_in_county is GIS_ACRES times that share.
limits: FRAP is incomplete: some perimeters are missing, duplicated or over-generalized (CAL FIRE's own caveat).
A perimeter is the final outline; the month is when the fire started, though large fires can burn into the next month.
Unburned islands inside a perimeter are counted as burned.
The layer includes some fires mapped across the Oregon and Nevada lines; they count wherever they reach a California hexagon.
Perimeters with no alarm or containment date in 2001-2025 cannot be placed in a month and are left out (see perimeters_dropped).

firms_inside.note: inside a >=1,000 acre perimeter, between the day before alarm and the day after containment (alarm + 90 days if no containment date)

large.source: CAL FIRE FRAP, California Fire Perimeters (all)
